We have search results: list of templates. Need to pick the appropriate one that applies to our target molecule. The target is a complex molecule with sulfonamide, aromatic, etc. The reaction of interest is amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine. The template likely is generic: amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine. Among results, look at retro_smarts_template. For example, entry 659569: retro_smarts_template '[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]>>O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]'. That seems to break amide to acid? It shows amide to acid? The forward direction is acid + amine -> amide. Retro direction is amide -> acid + amine. That seems appropriate. The template likely works for any amide attached to alkene? Our target has C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring via N attached to aromatic amine? Actually structure: .../C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So amide carbonyl attached to an aniline (aryl amine). The template may apply.

We need to apply the template to the target molecule to get precursors. Use apply_template with molecule_smiles and template_id (template_hash? Or template_id?). The search result includes template_hash and reaction_id. The tool apply_template expects template_id (string). Likely we use template_hash. Let's pick the second entry (reaction_id 659569) with template_hash 'd762c4d0baefb98e33ed46162a1ecdb28f829f785d3ea96f6ff22fe392afcc78'. Use that.

We'll apply template.
